blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: Food Banks
blocks.body:
In many countries, food banks help people who cannot afford enough food. Supermarkets and farms give food that they cannot sell, such as vegetables with small marks or products that are close to their best-before dates. Volunteers then ( 18 ) to families in need.
Food banks solve two problems at once. First, they help people who are struggling with money. Second, they ( 19 ). In Japan, millions of tons of food that could still be eaten are thrown away every year.
However, running a food bank is not easy. Many food banks depend on volunteers and donations, and they often do not have enough space to store food. ( 20 ), some cities have started to support food banks by giving them free warehouses.

qs.ex: ボランティアが食べ物を必要な家族に「届ける」。
直後の文で「まだ食べられる食品が大量に捨てられている」と述べているので、「食品ロスを減らす」。
「保管場所が足りない」→「そのため、市が倉庫を提供し始めた」という因果関係です。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: The Return of the Night Train
blocks.body:
For many years, night trains in Europe were losing passengers. Cheap airlines made it possible to travel between big cities in just a few hours, and many night train services were stopped.
Recently, however, night trains have ( 21 ). One reason is that more people are worried about the environment. Trains produce much less carbon dioxide than planes for the same trip. Some travelers also enjoy ( 22 ). They can go to bed in one city and wake up in another, without spending money on a hotel.
Train companies have responded to this demand. They have bought new trains with more comfortable beds and private rooms. Still, night trains face challenges. Tickets can be ( 23 ), and building new trains costs a lot of money.

qs.ex: however(しかし)のあとで、環境への関心などから「再び人気になった」。
次の文の「ある都市で寝て別の都市で目覚める」が説明になっています。
Still(それでも)課題がある、という流れ。「飛行機より高いことがある」。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Paul Carter
To: Riverside Tennis Club members
Date: September 3
Subject: Changes to our practice schedule

Dear members,
I'm writing to tell you about some changes to our practice schedule. As you know, the city is going to repair the tennis courts at Riverside Park. The work will start on September 20 and will take about six weeks. During this time, we won't be able to use the courts.
Luckily, Greenfield High School has kindly agreed to let us use its courts on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Practice will start at 6:30 p.m. instead of 6 p.m., because the high school's tennis club uses the courts until then. The high school is about 15 minutes from the park by bus, and the number 8 bus stops right in front of the school gate.
Also, please note that the club's year-end party will be held at a restaurant this year, not at the park. I'll send you more information about the party next month.
Best regards,
Paul Carter
Coach, Riverside Tennis Club

qs.q: Why will the club members not be able to use the courts at Riverside Park?
o: The park will close for the winter.
A high school will use the courts.
The city will build a new park.
qs.ex: the city is going to repair the tennis courts とあります。

qs.q: Practice at Greenfield High School will start at 6:30 p.m. because
o: the bus arrives at that time.
the high school's tennis club uses the courts until then.
the members asked for a later time.
qs.ex: because the high school's tennis club uses the courts until then とあります。

qs.q: What does Paul say about the year-end party?
o: It will be held at a restaurant.
It will be held at the high school.
It has been canceled this year.
Members should send him their ideas.
qs.ex: the club's year-end party will be held at a restaurant this year とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Why Do We Get Jet Lag?
blocks.body:
Many people who fly long distances suffer from jet lag. After crossing several time zones, they feel sleepy during the day and cannot sleep at night. They may also have headaches or feel hungry at strange times.
Jet lag happens because of our body clock. Inside our brain, there is a system that tells our body when to sleep and when to wake up. This body clock usually follows a cycle of about 24 hours, and it is set mainly by sunlight. When we suddenly arrive in a place where the sun rises and sets at different times, our body clock needs several days to adjust.
Interestingly, many people find that flying east is harder than flying west. Scientists believe that this is because most people's body clocks naturally run a little longer than 24 hours. When we fly west, our day becomes longer, which is easy for the body. When we fly east, our day becomes shorter, and the body has to work harder to catch up.
There are some ways to reduce jet lag. Experts suggest changing your sleeping time a little before the trip. After you arrive, you should go outside and get sunlight during the day. It is also a good idea to avoid long naps, even if you feel very tired.

qs.q: What is one effect of jet lag?
o: People feel sleepy during the day.
People lose their sense of direction.
qs.ex: they feel sleepy during the day and cannot sleep at night とあります。

qs.q: Our body clock is set mainly by
qs.ex: it is set mainly by sunlight とあります。

qs.q: Why do many people find flying east harder than flying west?
o: Planes flying east are usually slower.
There is less sunlight in the east.
Their body clocks naturally run a little longer than 24 hours.
They usually sleep on planes flying west.
qs.ex: 体内時計がもともと24時間より少し長いので、1日が短くなる東向きはつらいのです。

qs.q: What do experts suggest doing after arriving?
qs.ex: you should go outside and get sunlight during the day とあります。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Jet lag only happens on short flights.
Our body clock needs several days to adjust to a new time zone.
Flying west makes our day shorter.
Experts say long naps are the best way to stop jet lag.
qs.ex: our body clock needs several days to adjust とあります。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は25語〜35語です。
parts.body:
In some countries, a growing number of companies are allowing their workers to bring their dogs to the office. Some companies even have special areas where dogs can play.
Supporters say that having dogs at work makes employees feel less stressed. Also, workers have to take their dogs for short walks, so they take breaks and move their bodies more often.
On the other hand, not everyone likes dogs. Some people are afraid of them or have allergies. In addition, dogs can be noisy and may make it difficult for other workers to concentrate.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Some companies let workers bring dogs to the office. This can reduce stress and help workers take breaks. However, some people fear dogs or have allergies, and dogs can disturb others.
checks: 第1段落(会社に犬を連れて来られる)の内容が入っている
第2段落(良い点:ストレス軽減・休憩)の内容が入っている
第3段落(悪い点:苦手な人・アレルギー・うるさい)の内容が入っている
本文の文をそのまま写さず、自分の言葉で短くまとめている
語数が25〜35語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。

QUESTION
Do you think high schools should allow students to have part-time jobs?
rules: 語数の目安は50語〜60語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
QUESTIONに答えていない場合や、内容がQUESTIONからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I think high schools should allow students to have part-time jobs. First, students can learn how hard it is to earn money, so they will use money more carefully. Second, working with adults helps students improve their communication skills, which will be useful in the future. Therefore, I agree with this idea.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
理由に具体的な説明がある
語数が50〜60語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, I'd like to open a bank account.
Certainly. Do you have some ID with you?
I'm afraid we need a passport or a driver's license.
Oh. I'll come back tomorrow with my passport.
items.q: What will the woman do tomorrow?
o: Bring her passport to the bank.
items.ex: I'll come back tomorrow with my passport. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me, is this the right platform for the express to Kyoto?
It was, but the platform was changed this morning. It now leaves from Platform 7.
Oh, thanks. How long does it take to get there?
items.q: What is the man's problem?
o: He is on the wrong platform.
items.ex: 発車ホームが変わったので、今いるホームはちがいます。

lines: I have to give a presentation in English tomorrow, and I'm really nervous.
Why don't you practice in front of me tonight?
items.q: What will the woman do tonight?
items.ex: 彼女の前で練習するよう提案しています。

lines: Hello. I ordered a pizza about an hour ago, but it still hasn't arrived.
I'm very sorry, sir. Our driver had a problem with his car. It should be there in ten minutes.
We'll give you a free drink for the trouble.
items.q: Why is the pizza late?
o: The man gave the wrong address.
The driver had a car problem.
The man ordered the wrong pizza.
items.ex: Our driver had a problem with his car. と言っています。

lines: Dad, can you drive me to the concert tonight?
Sorry, I have to work late. Can't you take the train?
The concert ends at ten, and the last train leaves at ten fifteen.
Then ask your mom. She'll be home by seven.
items.q: What does the father suggest?
items.ex: Then ask your mom. と言っています。

lines: Did you hear that Lisa won the speech contest?
Really? That's amazing. She practiced every day for two months.
She'll go to the national contest in Tokyo next month.
Let's give her a card to say congratulations.
items.q: What will Lisa do next month?
o: Give a card to her friends.
items.ex: She'll go to the national contest in Tokyo next month. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me. I'm looking for a gift for my father. He likes cooking.
How about this cookbook? It has many easy recipes.
Hmm, he already has a lot of cookbooks.
Then how about this apron? It's very popular.
items.q: What will the woman buy?
items.ex: 料理本はたくさん持っているので、エプロンにしました。

lines: Ms. Jones, I'd like to change from the soccer club to the art club.
I hurt my knee, and the doctor said I shouldn't play soccer for a year.
I see. I'll talk to the art club teacher.
items.q: Why does Ken want to change clubs?
o: He wants to become an artist.
His friend is in the art club.
items.ex: ひざのけがで1年間サッカーができないからです。

lines: Honey, the washing machine isn't working again.
Again? It's only three years old.
Should we call the repair shop?
Let's just buy a new one. Repairs are too expensive.
items.q: What does the man want to do?
items.ex: Let's just buy a new one. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me, does this museum have a café?
Yes, but it's closed today for cleaning. There's a restaurant across the street, though.
Can I come back into the museum after lunch?
Yes. Just show your ticket at the entrance.
items.q: What should the man do to come back into the museum?
items.ex: Just show your ticket at the entrance. と言っています。

lines: Jim, have you finished packing for the trip?
Almost. I can't find my sunglasses.
Did you check the car? You wore them when we went to the beach.
items.q: Where will Jim look for his sunglasses?
items.ex: 車を見てくると言っています。

lines: Hi, Sarah. Are you still looking for a part-time job?
Yes. Do you know of any?
My uncle's bakery needs someone on weekends.
That sounds great. Could you give me his phone number?
items.q: What does Sarah ask for?
items.ex: Could you give me his phone number? とたのんでいます。

lines: Welcome to Sky Airlines. May I see your passport?
Here you are. Can I have an aisle seat?
I'm sorry, only window seats are left.
items.q: Where will the man sit?
items.ex: 通路側は空いておらず、窓側の席になります。

lines: Mom, the school trip fee is due tomorrow.
Tomorrow? Why didn't you tell me earlier?
Sorry, I forgot. The letter was in my bag.
OK. I'll go to the bank in the morning.
items.q: Why is the mother surprised?
items.ex: 旅行の費用の支払いが明日までだと急に聞いたからです。

lines: How did your job interview go?
I think it went well. They asked a lot of questions about my experience.
When will you know the result?
They said they'd call me by Friday.
items.q: When will the man hear the result?
items.ex: They said they'd call me by Friday. と言っています。

lines: Tim loves taking photos of birds. Last spring, he entered a photo contest held by his city. He took more than 500 pictures at a lake near his house. In the end, his photo of a kingfisher won first prize, and it is now displayed at the city hall.
items.q: Where is Tim's photo displayed now?
items.ex: it is now displayed at the city hall とあります。

lines: Welcome aboard Flight 52 to Honolulu. Our flight time today will be about seven hours. Shortly after takeoff, we will serve drinks and a light meal. Please keep your seat belt fastened while you are seated.
items.q: What will happen shortly after takeoff?
o: Drinks and a light meal will be served.
The captain will make another announcement.
items.ex: Shortly after takeoff, we will serve drinks and a light meal. とあります。

lines: Pandas eat bamboo for most of the day. Although bamboo has little nutrition, pandas can survive by eating a large amount of it, sometimes more than 12 kilograms a day. Pandas also save energy by moving slowly and resting a lot.
items.q: How do pandas save energy?
items.ex: by moving slowly and resting a lot とあります。

lines: Maria moved to Japan from Brazil last year. At first, she could not read any kanji, so shopping was difficult. Her neighbor, Mrs. Ito, taught her some useful kanji every evening. Now Maria can read signs at the supermarket and even write her address in Japanese.
items.q: Who helped Maria learn kanji?
items.ex: Her neighbor, Mrs. Ito, taught her some useful kanji とあります。

lines: Attention, all students. Because of the typhoon, all afternoon classes are canceled today. Students should go home by 1 p.m. Club activities are also canceled. Please be careful on your way home.
items.q: What should students do?
o: Stay at school until the evening.
items.ex: Students should go home by 1 p.m. とあります。

lines: Ken is a high school student who wants to become a vet. Every Saturday, he volunteers at an animal hospital. He cleans the cages and feeds the animals. He says that seeing the doctors work has made his dream even stronger.
items.q: What does Ken do on Saturdays?
o: He volunteers at an animal hospital.
He studies at a cram school.
He works at a pet shop.
He takes his dog to the doctor.
items.ex: Every Saturday, he volunteers at an animal hospital. とあります。

lines: In the past, ice cream was a luxury that only rich people could enjoy, because keeping it cold was very difficult. After freezers were invented, ice cream became cheaper and easier to make. Today, it is one of the most popular desserts in the world.
items.q: Why was ice cream a luxury in the past?
o: It was made only in Italy.
It was hard to keep it cold.
items.ex: keeping it cold was very difficult とあります。

lines: Thank you for calling Green Valley Hotel. Our front desk is busy right now. If you want to make a reservation, please press 1. If you want to change or cancel a reservation, please press 2. For other questions, please stay on the line.
items.q: What should callers do to cancel a reservation?
items.ex: change or cancel は2を押します。

lines: Sophie used to buy a coffee every morning on her way to work. She realized that she was spending more than 100 dollars a month on coffee. Now she makes coffee at home and brings it in a bottle. She is saving the money to go on a trip to Spain.
items.q: Why does Sophie make coffee at home now?
items.ex: コーヒー代を節約してスペイン旅行のお金をためています。

lines: Many cities around the world are planting trees and plants on the roofs of buildings. These "green roofs" help keep buildings cool in summer, so less energy is needed for air conditioning. They also give birds and insects a place to live.
items.q: What is one benefit of green roofs?
o: They produce fruit for the city.
They reduce the need for air conditioning.
They keep buildings warm in summer.
items.ex: less energy is needed for air conditioning とあります。

lines: Last month, Hiroshi started learning to play the drums. He practices at a music studio because his apartment is small and noisy instruments are not allowed there. His goal is to play in a band with his friends at the school festival.
items.q: Why does Hiroshi practice at a music studio?
o: Noisy instruments are not allowed in his apartment.
items.ex: アパートでは大きな音の楽器が禁止されているからです。

lines: Attention, shoppers. A child named Ben has been found near the toy section. He is wearing a red jacket and is about five years old. If you are his parent, please come to the service counter on the first floor.
items.q: Where should Ben's parent go?
items.ex: please come to the service counter on the first floor とあります。

lines: Octopuses are very intelligent animals. In experiments, some octopuses have learned to open jars to get food inside. They can also change the color of their skin in less than a second to hide from enemies.
items.q: What can octopuses do to hide from enemies?
o: Change the color of their skin.
items.ex: change the color of their skin ... to hide from enemies とあります。

lines: Lucy's family always went to the beach for summer vacation. This year, Lucy suggested going camping in the mountains instead. At first, her parents were not sure, but they ended up enjoying hiking and cooking outside. Now they want to go camping every year.
items.q: How did Lucy's parents feel about the camping trip in the end?
o: They wanted to go to the beach instead.
items.ex: ended up enjoying hiking and cooking outside(結局楽しんだ)とあります。

lines: Many people throw away old smartphones. However, these phones contain small amounts of valuable metals such as gold and silver. For the Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games, the medals were made from metals collected from old phones and other small electronic devices.
items.q: What were the Tokyo 2020 medals made from?
o: Metals collected from old electronic devices.
items.ex: 古い携帯電話などの小型電子機器から集めた金属で作られました。
